verses.text: Joshua got up early in the morning; and they moved from Shittim, and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel. They camped there before they crossed over.
After three days, the officers went through the middle of the camp;
and they commanded the people, saying, “When you see the ark of Yahweh your God’s covenant, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then leave your place, and follow it.

Yet there shall be a space between you and it of about two thousand cubits  by measure — don’t come closer to it — that you may know the way by which you must go; for you have not passed this way before.”
Joshua said to the people, “Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you.”
Joshua spoke to the priests, saying, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and cross over before the people.” They took up the ark of the covenant, and went before the people.
Yahweh said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, saying, ‘When you come to the brink of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.’”
Joshua said to the children of Israel, “Come here, and hear the words of Yahweh your God.”

Joshua said, “By this you shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Perizzite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Jebusite out from before you.
Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord  of all the earth passes over before you into the Jordan.
Now therefore take twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, for every tribe a man.

It shall be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of Yahweh, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The waters that come down from above shall stand in one heap.”
When the people moved from their tents to pass over the Jordan, the priests who bore the ark of the covenant being before the people,

and when those who bore the ark had come to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bore the ark had dipped in the edge of the water (for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest),

the waters which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap, a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over near Jericho.

The priests who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan; and all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the nation had passed completely over the Jordan.

footnotes.content: Joshua rises early—the mark of a leader ready to move. They've camped at Shittim, and now face the Jordan between them and the promised land. How much like us: poised at the edge of what God has called us to, waiting, watching, ready.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three days of waiting. Not a slow drag—they're being deliberate, letting officers move through the camp with word. I've learned that the Lord often uses the space between His promise and His fulfillment to shape our faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ark of Yahweh is to lead. Follow it. That one command holds all of faith—not the map, not the officers' wisdom, but the tangible presence of God's covenant going before us. Everything hinges on that.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep your distance—about two thousand cubits, they're told. There's mercy in that distance: it lets them see the ark, follow its path, learn the way without being consumed by too-nearness. Even obedience has room to breathe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sanctify yourselves. Joshua calls them to be set apart, readied. Wonders are coming—tomorrow, he says. But first, the heart must be prepared. The Lord doesn't work in unwilling soil.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests take up the ark and go before the people. Leadership isn't holding back—it's stepping forward into the unknown, bearing what is holy. The people see and follow. That's always been the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh promises Joshua: I will magnify you before all Israel, just as I was with Moses. Joshua needs to hear this—a young man stepping into an old man's sandals. The Lord says: I haven't abandoned this people. I am still here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Command the priests to stand still in the Jordan. Stand still. In a rushing river about to flood. The word is obey first, understand later. That's when miracles happen—when we stop calculating and simply do what we're told.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Come here and hear the words of Yahweh. Not scattered whispers, but a gathering—all of them called to listen together. God speaks plainly to a people willing to draw close and pay attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By this you shall know that the living God is among you. Joshua names seven nations—a full accounting of what stands against them. But the sign isn't the army's strength; it's God's presence. That's always been the difference between us and the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passes over before you. All the earth—He's Lord of it all, not just Canaan. That reframing steadies the heart. Whatever we face, He has already claimed it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twelve men, one from each tribe. A memorial is being called for, though they don't know it yet. The Lord thinks ahead—He wants witnesses, stones set up to say: He was here. He did this.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When the priests' feet dip in the water, the Jordan will be cut off. Not before—after. The obedience comes first, the miracle second. That order matters. Faith that acts, then sees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people move from their tents toward the Jordan, the priests and the ark leading. The entire nation—young and old, strong and weak—rising together, following. What courage it takes to leave shelter and step toward water.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Jordan overflows—harvest time, the waters at their worst. They're not crossing at low water; they're crossing when it's fullest, when the danger is greatest. God often waits until the obstacle is hardest to see His glory more clearly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The waters stand in a heap far off—at Adam, toward Zarethan. A dry path opens through the middle. Every person walks across solid ground where moments before was a raging river. They will remember this their whole lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests stand firm on dry ground in the Jordan while all Israel crosses. Readers today hear an echo of a shepherd holding steady in the waters of our own crossings, His feet planted where we would drown. He stands so we can walk through.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
